subject: AcmeHealth - Private VPC dataflow & privacy follow-up

Subject: AcmeHealth - Private VPC dataflow & privacy follow-up

Hi Emily / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really appreciated the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the Private/VPC deployment requirements you mentioned: 

Summary from today
- Goal: Run inference on Acme Health patient-facing workloads without any patient-identifiable data leaving your environment.
- Preferred deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed network and strict egress controls.
- Key concerns raised: PII/PHI handling, data retention limits, logging/audit visibility, and on-prem/air-gapped constraints for certain environments.

Open items / requests from your side
1) Confirmation of retention windows for logs and model inputs (you mentioned 90 days for inputs, 12 months for audit logs?).
2) Any required encryption standards or KMS provider constraints (e.g., AWS KMS vs. HSM).
3) Network constraints: IP allowlist, specific ports, and whether a private peering/VPN or AWS Transit Gateway is preferred.
4) Do you require a fully air-gapped option for any workloads, or is VPC with restricted egress sufficient for now?

What I attached
- redwood_private_vpc_checklist.xlsx (short checklist for networking, certs, and presales items)
- Link to a draft dataflow diagram to start from: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cAcmeHealthDataflow

Proposed next steps
- Vivek (CC'd), our lead solutions engineer, can do a detailed network/dataflow review next week. Can you share a time that works?
- If helpful, please loop in whoever owns your security/compliance questionnaire — we can prepare a SOC2 summary and sample configs.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmehealth.com>, Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - Private VPC dataflow & privacy follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from Security & Platform: 

1) Data residency / PII: For production patient workloads, we cannot allow any PHI/PII to be transferred to external networks. That means inference must run in our VPC and any stored inputs (for debugging or caching) must be encrypted and retained for a maximum of 90 days unless otherwise approved.

2) Logging: Audit logs (access, model version, request metadata) need to be retained for 12 months and stored in our centralized logging account. We also need a way to export logs to our SIEM (Splunk) via a push or S3 export.

3) Egress & network: We require strict egress controls. Preferred setup is either (a) customer-managed VPN to Redwood presales endpoints + allowlist, or (b) a private peering arrangement. No direct public internet egress is allowed from inference nodes.

4) On-prem/air-gapped: Some pilot workloads (research) will need an air-gapped option. For now, we want a VPC deployment for production and an air-gapped package for research evaluation.

5) Evidence: Please provide your most recent SOC 2 report/summary and a draft dataflow diagram showing ingress/egress, where caching occurs, and where logs are forwarded.

We can do a technical review with Vivek on July 15 or 16 — Tom and I are available in the mornings.

Thanks,

Emily Carter
Head of Platform Security, Acme Health
emily.carter@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acmehealth.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - Private VPC dataflow & privacy follow-up

Emily — thanks, great notes. Replying with the items you requested and proposed timeline. Quoting your ask inline where helpful.

1) Data residency / PII- We confirm Redwood Private can be deployed inside your VPC so inference and any model inputs remain in your account. By default, we do not persist user inputs outside the compute unless caching is enabled — caching is opt-in and can be configured to be ephemeral or stored in a customer-controlled S3 bucket with lifecycle rules. For production we recommend disabling caching of raw inputs; we can provide a hashed-prefix cache if needed.

2) Logging- Audit logs (request metadata, model version, operator actions) can be forwarded to your logging account via S3 or a direct push to your Splunk HTTP intake. Retention and lifecycle policies are controlled by your account; Redwood will not retain logs beyond what you configure. We can include a logging playbook as part of the deployment.

3) Egress & network- Options we support: 
  - Customer-managed VPN (IPSec) to Redwood presales endpoints so nodes have no public egress.
  - AWS PrivateLink / VPC peering for direct connectivity.
  - For stricter controls, we can recommend an inline NAT/proxy that only allows connections to Redwood update endpoints for kernel patches; otherwise software updates can be pushed via your ops channel.

4) Air-gapped/on-prem- We offer an on-prem/air-gapped package for evaluation. It includes an installer and offline bundle for model weights and runtime. That package requires a separate support agreement and a short-week integration plan; I added a note in the attached checklist.

5) Evidence & attachments- Attached: acme_vpc_dataflow_diagram.pdf (draft showing where inference runs, KV cache boundaries, and log export points).
  - SOC2: our latest SOC2 summary is available here: https://redwood.ai/soc2-report/latest (we can provide a full report under NDA).

6) Proposed next steps / meeting- Vivek can lead a 60-minute network/dataflow deep-dive. Proposed slots: Thu Jul 16, 09:00-10:00 PT or Fri Jul 17, 09:00-10:00 PT. Please confirm which works or propose alternatives.

I left detailed notes in the attached checklist and highlighted the items that require action from Acme (network contact, SIEM endpoint, and retention policy confirmation).

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
